## Teaching points

1. Emphysematous pyelonephritis occurs mostly in people with diabetes or urinary obstruction; suspect it when apparent pyelonephritis comes with shock, severe acidosis or no response to antibiotics.
2. On bedside ultrasound, gas appears as echogenic foci with 'dirty' shadowing and reverberation artifact, unlike the clean, echo-free shadow of a stone.
3. CT confirms the diagnosis and maps the gas (for example by the Huang–Tseng classes), which guides the choice between drainage and nephrectomy.
4. Antibiotics alone carry a much higher mortality than antibiotics plus percutaneous drainage or nephrectomy; involve urology at once and reassess early.
5. Resuscitate sepsis-induced hypoperfusion with at least 30 mL/kg of crystalloid in the first 3 hours, with frequent reassessment (Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021).
